slot.brief: Given a complex ion (with ligands listed), determine its hybridisation/geometry/spin state using CFT — figure-free but with structural formula of the complex in the question.

stem: The spin-only magnetic moment of [Co(NH3)6]2+ is closest to

verdicts.working: Co²⁺ is d⁷; [Co(NH₃)₆]²⁺ is high-spin with 3 unpaired electrons. μ = √[3(3+2)] = √15 ≈ 3.87 BM.

working:
Co2+ is 3d7. NH3 is a strong-field ligand for many M3+ ions, but for Co2+ the pairing energy is greater than the crystal field splitting, so the complex remains high spin. Configuration: t2g5 eg2, giving 3 unpaired electrons. Spin-only magnetic moment = sqrt(3 * (3 + 2)) = sqrt(15) = 3.87 BM. Hence option C.

Independent check: Co²⁺ is d⁷; [Co(NH₃)₆]²⁺ is high-spin with 3 unpaired electrons. μ = √[3(3+2)] = √15 ≈ 3.87 BM.
solution:
Co$^{2+}$ is $3d^7$; in this octahedral complex it is high-spin, with $3$ unpaired electrons.
$$\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}=\sqrt{3(3+2)}=\sqrt{15}\approx 3.87\text{ BM}$$
